For worship. You are fully known by God, and fully loved. And one day you will see him face to face. Rejoice in that hope.
verseByVerse.note: Mirrors were made of polished metal and gave a dim, imperfect reflection; Corinth was famous for its bronze work. The ESV notes that “dimly” is literally “in a riddle.”

parallels.desc: with him I speak mouth to mouth, clearly, and not in riddles

verseByVerse.quote: So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love.
verseByVerse.commentary:
So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love.

So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three. Key words. “Abide” (menō, remain, last). Unlike the gifts, these three are permanent features of the Christian life. Paul often groups them (1 Thessalonians 1:3; 5:8; Colossians 1:4–5). Faith trusts God; hope looks forward to what he has promised; love gives itself to God and others.

But the greatest of these is love. Key words. Why the greatest? Faith will become sight, and hope will be fulfilled (Romans 8:24; 2 Corinthians 5:7); but love goes on forever. And love is what God himself is (1 John 4:8, 16). God does not have faith or hope, but he is love. Love is the bond of the age to come.

What it does not mean. It does not mean faith and hope are unimportant. We are justified by faith alone (Romans 5:1), and hope is our anchor (Hebrews 6:19). But love is the goal of everything (1 Timothy 1:5).

In a sentence. So these three remain: faith, hope and love. And the greatest of them is love.

On a Tuesday. At the end of today, ask not just: did I believe? did I hope? But: did I love?

13.text: <sup>1</sup>If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal.<sup>2</sup>And if I have prophetic powers, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.<sup>3</sup>If I give away all I have, and if I deliver up my body to be burned, but have not love, I gain nothing.<sup>4</sup>Love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant<sup>5</sup>or rude. It does not insist on its own way; it is not irritable or resentful;<sup>6</sup>it does not rejoice at wrongdoing, but rejoices with the truth.<sup>7</sup>Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.<sup>8</sup>Love never ends. As for prophecies, they will pass away; as for tongues, they will cease; as for knowledge, it will pass away.<sup>9</sup>For we know in part and we prophesy in part,<sup>10</sup>but when the perfect comes, the partial will pass away.<sup>11</sup>When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I gave up childish ways.<sup>12</sup>For now we see in a mirror dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I have been fully known.<sup>13</sup>So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love.

14.title: Prophecy, Tongues, and the Order of Worship
14.overview:
Having shown that love is the way all gifts must be used, Paul applies it to the Corinthians’ worship, which had become noisy and confusing as many people spoke in tongues at once. His test is simple: what builds up the church? Tongues spoken without interpretation build up only the speaker, because no one else understands; prophecy, spoken in ordinary language, strengthens, encourages and comforts everyone. Like a flute that plays no recognisable tune, or a bugle with an uncertain call, unintelligible speech helps nobody, and a visitor cannot even say “Amen” to a prayer he does not understand. Paul himself speaks in tongues more than all of them, but in church he would rather say five words people can understand than ten thousand in a tongue.

He quotes Isaiah, where foreign speech was a sign of God’s judgement on unbelieving Israel, and warns that a visitor who walks into a room full of tongues will think they are mad, whereas prophecy may expose his heart and bring him to worship God. Then he gives practical rules. Each person may contribute, a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue or an interpretation, but everything must build others up. Only two or three should speak in tongues, in turn, with interpretation; two or three prophets should speak and the others weigh what they say. God is a God of peace, not disorder. Women should keep silent in this setting, apparently in the weighing of prophecies. Paul’s instructions are the Lord’s command, and everything should be done decently and in order.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Paul tells them to make love their aim, and to desire spiritual gifts eagerly, especially prophecy. Someone who speaks in a tongue speaks to God, not to people, because no one understands; he utters mysteries by the Spirit. But someone who prophesies speaks to people, building them up, encouraging and comforting them. The tongue-speaker edifies himself, but the prophet edifies the church. Paul would like every one of them to speak in tongues, but he would rather they prophesied. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless someone interprets, so that the church may be built up.
verseByVerse.theology:
Intelligibility as a Prerequisite for Edification

Paul’s governing principle for corporate worship — intelligibility — has deep theological roots. The God who speaks is a God who communicates; the Word became flesh precisely to be heard and understood. Worship that renders the word of God inaccessible to the gathered community is, at a structural level, working against the grain of the incarnation. The Reformers’ insistence on vernacular worship (against the Latin Mass) was an application of precisely this principle: if the people cannot understand what is being said and done, they cannot be edified.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: The Corinthian preference for tongues in corporate worship was driven by the same status-seeking that produced the faction fights: tongues was the impressive gift, the spectacular performance. Paul’s preference for prophecy is a preference for the communal over the spectacular, the edifying over the impressive. Now: The principle of intelligibility has applications beyond tongues: jargon-laden sermons, inaccessible liturgy, and culturally opaque worship practices all fail the same criterion. Does the person who attends understand what is happening? Are they being built up?

verseByVerse.quote: Pursue love, and earnestly desire the spiritual gifts, especially that you may prophesy. For one who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men but to God; for no one understands him, but he utters mysteries in the Spirit.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Pursue love, and earnestly desire the spiritual gifts, especially that you may prophesy. For one who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men but to God; for no one understands him, but he utters mysteries in the Spirit.

Meaning first. 1 Corinthians 14 applies the love of chapter 13 to the Corinthians’ worship. Their gatherings were chaotic: many speaking in tongues at once, with no interpretation, so that no one understood and outsiders thought them mad. Paul’s principle is that everything in worship must build up the church, and only what is understood can build up. So prophecy, which speaks God’s word intelligibly, is greater than uninterpreted tongues (vv. 1–5). Unintelligible sounds are as useless as a bugle with no clear note; pray and sing with the mind as well as the spirit (vv. 6–19). Tongues without interpretation are a sign of judgement on unbelievers, while prophecy convicts them and brings them to worship (vv. 20–25). Then come practical rules: two or three speakers at most, one at a time, with interpretation and weighing; women are not to take part in judging what is said; and all things must be done decently and in order, because God is a God of peace (vv. 26–40).

Pursue love. Key words. “Pursue” (diōkō, chase, hunt). Love from chapter 13 is the aim of everything.

And earnestly desire the spiritual gifts, especially that you may prophesy. Key words. Love does not cancel gifts; it directs them. Prophecy is especially to be desired because it builds others up.

For one who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men but to God. Key words. Without interpretation, a tongue is addressed to God, in prayer or praise, not to the congregation.

For no one understands him, but he utters mysteries in the Spirit. Key words. “Understands” is literally hears. No one grasps it. “Mysteries” here means things hidden from the hearers, not understood. “In the Spirit” (or in his spirit, as the ESV notes): by the Spirit’s enabling.

Where Christians differ: what were tongues? Some think the Corinthian tongues were ecstatic, non-human speech; others that they were real human languages as at Pentecost. Verdict: At Pentecost, tongues were known human languages, understood by foreigners (Acts 2:6–11). Paul’s own analogy here is foreign languages (vv. 10–11), and interpretation means translation. So the most natural reading is that tongues were real languages the speaker had not learned. Paul’s mention of tongues of angels (13:1) is a hypothetical extreme, not a description of the gift.

What it does not mean. It does not mean tongues were useless. Paul values them (v. 18). But in the gathered church, they must be interpreted.

In a sentence. Make love your aim, and eagerly seek the gifts of the Spirit, above all prophecy. Someone speaking in a tongue is speaking to God, not to people, since no one understands; by the Spirit he speaks things hidden from his hearers.

On a Tuesday. In all your speech this week, at church and elsewhere, aim to be understood and to build others up.

verseByVerse.quote: On the other hand, the one who prophesies speaks to people for their upbuilding and encouragement and consolation.
verseByVerse.commentary:
On the other hand, the one who prophesies speaks to people for their upbuilding and encouragement and consolation.

On the other hand, the one who prophesies speaks to people. Key words. Prophecy is addressed to the congregation, in their language.

For their upbuilding. Key words. “Upbuilding” (oikodomē): building up in faith and maturity, the key word of the chapter (vv. 3, 4, 5, 12, 17, 26).

And encouragement. Key words. “Encouragement” (paraklēsis): exhortation, urging on, comfort.

And consolation. Key words. “Consolation” (paramythia): comfort for the grieving and discouraged.

What it does not mean. It does not mean prophecy was only encouragement and never correction. It could expose sin (vv. 24–25). And it does not mean prophecy is the same as preaching, though they share these purposes.

In a sentence. But someone who prophesies speaks to people, to strengthen, urge on and comfort them.

For worship. Thank God for the ministry of the word that builds you up, urges you on and comforts you.

verseByVerse.quote: The one who speaks in a tongue builds up himself, but the one who prophesies builds up the church. Now I want you all to speak in tongues, but even more to prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless someone interprets, so that the church may be built up.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The one who speaks in a tongue builds up himself, but the one who prophesies builds up the church. Now I want you all to speak in tongues, but even more to prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless someone interprets, so that the church may be built up.

The one who speaks in a tongue builds up himself. Key words. The speaker may be edified in some way, perhaps through the experience of praising God, even without understanding the words. But this is not the purpose of gifts, which are for the common good (12:7).

But the one who prophesies builds up the church. Key words. Prophecy serves everyone.

Now I want you all to speak in tongues, but even more to prophesy. Key words. Paul does not despise tongues. But he does not mean all will (12:30); it is a wish, like his wish that all were single (7:7).

The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless someone interprets. Key words. Greater: more useful to the church. Interpreted tongues are equivalent to prophecy in their effect.

So that the church may be built up. Key words. The test for everything.

What it does not mean. It does not mean self-edification is wrong. It means public worship is for building up others.

In a sentence. Someone who speaks in a tongue strengthens himself, but someone who prophesies strengthens the church. Paul would be glad if all of you spoke in tongues, but gladder still if you prophesied. Prophecy does more good than tongues, unless the tongue is interpreted so that the church is built up.

On a Tuesday. When you serve in church, ask: does this build others up, or mainly me?

parallels.desc: would that all the LORD’s people were prophets!

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Paul asks what good it would do them if he came speaking in tongues and brought no revelation, knowledge, prophecy or teaching. Even lifeless instruments, a flute or a harp, must play distinct notes to be recognised, and if a trumpet sounds an unclear call, who will prepare for battle? It is the same with them: unintelligible speech is talking into the air. There are many languages in the world, all meaningful, but if Paul does not understand a language he and the speaker are foreigners to each other. Since they are eager for spiritual gifts, they should seek to excel in those that build up the church. So anyone who speaks in a tongue should pray for the power to interpret. If Paul prays in a tongue, his spirit prays but his mind is unproductive. So he will pray and sing both with his spirit and with his mind. Otherwise, how can an outsider say “Amen” to his thanksgiving if he does not know what is being said? He may give thanks well, but the other person is not built up. Paul thanks God that he speaks in tongues more than all of them, but in church he would rather speak five words that teach others than ten thousand in a tongue.
verseByVerse.theology:
The Corporate Criterion and the Nature of Worship

Paul’s insistence on intelligibility in corporate worship reflects a deep theological conviction about the nature of Christian assembly: it is not a private spiritual experience shared simultaneously by many individuals but a genuinely corporate event in which the whole body is built up together. Worship is not merely my encounter with God in the presence of other people; it is our encounter with God as a body. This corporate dimension requires intelligibility: I cannot say “Amen” to what I cannot understand, and a community of “Amens” is the sign that the body is genuinely worshipping together.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: The Corinthian tongues-enthusiasts were essentially importing an individual spiritual practice into the corporate meeting without consideration for the community’s ability to participate. Paul’s five-to-ten-thousand ratio is not a rule to be calculated but a principle to be embodied: always ask, in corporate worship, whether what is done can be received and responded to by the whole community. Now: The principle applies to any element of worship that prioritises the experience of some over the edification of all.

verseByVerse.quote: Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
verseByVerse.commentary:
Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?

Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues. Key words. Paul uses himself as an example. Suppose he visited and only spoke in tongues.

How will I benefit you. Key words. What good would it do?

Unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching? Key words. Four intelligible forms of speech. Revelation and prophecy: messages from God. Knowledge and teaching: explanation of truth. These benefit the hearers because they can be understood.

What it does not mean. It does not mean experience has no place in worship. It means understanding must be central.

In a sentence. Brothers and sisters, if Paul came to you speaking in tongues, what use would he be to you, unless he brought you some revelation, knowledge, prophecy or teaching?

For worship. Thank God for clear teaching in your church. Pray for your preachers to be clear.

verseByVerse.quote: If even lifeless instruments, such as the flute or the harp, do not give distinct notes, how will anyone know what is played? And if the bugle gives an indistinct sound, who will get ready for battle?
verseByVerse.commentary:
If even lifeless instruments, such as the flute or the harp, do not give distinct notes, how will anyone know what is played? And if the bugle gives an indistinct sound, who will get ready for battle?

If even lifeless instruments, such as the flute or the harp, do not give distinct notes, how will anyone know what is played? Key words. Music needs distinct notes to make a recognisable tune. A random noise is not music.

And if the bugle gives an indistinct sound, who will get ready for battle? Key words. A trumpet sounded signals to soldiers in battle: advance, retreat, gather. An unclear signal leaves soldiers confused. In worship, unclear speech leaves the church unprepared.

What it does not mean. It does not mean instruments are wrong in worship. Paul uses them as an illustration.

In a sentence. Even lifeless instruments like the flute or harp: if they do not sound distinct notes, how can anyone tell the tune? And if the trumpet’s call is unclear, who will get ready for battle?

On a Tuesday. Speak clearly about Christ. An unclear witness leaves people confused.
verseByVerse.note: A trumpet sounded signals to soldiers in battle.

verseByVerse.quote: So with yourselves, if with your tongue you utter speech that is not intelligible, how will anyone know what is said? For you will be speaking into the air. There are doubtless many different languages in the world, and none is without meaning, but if I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be a foreigner to the speaker and the speaker a foreigner to me.
verseByVerse.commentary:
So with yourselves, if with your tongue you utter speech that is not intelligible, how will anyone know what is said? For you will be speaking into the air. There are doubtless many different languages in the world, and none is without meaning, but if I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be a foreigner to the speaker and the speaker a foreigner to me.

So with yourselves, if with your tongue you utter speech that is not intelligible. Key words. “Intelligible” (eusēmos, clear, distinct).

How will anyone know what is said? For you will be speaking into the air. Key words. Wasted words. Like beating the air (9:26).

There are doubtless many different languages in the world, and none is without meaning. Key words. “Languages” (phōnai, voices, sounds). Every human language means something.

But if I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be a foreigner to the speaker and the speaker a foreigner to me. Key words. “Foreigner” (barbaros, barbarian: someone whose speech sounds like bar-bar to Greek ears). Uninterpreted tongues make church members foreigners to each other. The comparison with human languages supports the view that tongues were real languages.

What it does not mean. It does not mean tongues were meaningless. They had meaning, but the hearers could not understand it without interpretation.

In a sentence. It is the same with you. Unless your tongue speaks words people can understand, how will they know what you are saying? You will just be talking into the air. There are many languages in the world, and each has meaning; but if Paul does not know the language, he and the speaker are foreigners to each other.

For worship. Thank God for Bible translators who make his word understandable in every language.

verseByVerse.quote: So with yourselves, since you are eager for manifestations of the Spirit, strive to excel in building up the church.
verseByVerse.commentary:
So with yourselves, since you are eager for manifestations of the Spirit, strive to excel in building up the church.

So with yourselves, since you are eager for manifestations of the Spirit. Key words. Literally, zealots for spirits. The Corinthians were enthusiastic about spiritual experiences.

Strive to excel in building up the church. Key words. Redirect your zeal. Do not seek gifts for your own spirituality, but to build others up. “Excel” (perisseuō, abound, overflow).

What it does not mean. It does not mean zeal is bad. Paul channels it rightly.

In a sentence. So since you are keen on the Spirit’s gifts, aim to overflow in the ones that build up the church.

On a Tuesday. Channel your enthusiasm for God into building up others in your church.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore, one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret. For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays but my mind is unfruitful. What am I to do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will pray with my mind also; I will sing praise with my spirit, but I will sing with my mind also.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Therefore, one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret. For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays but my mind is unfruitful. What am I to do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will pray with my mind also; I will sing praise with my spirit, but I will sing with my mind also.

Therefore, one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret. Key words. Ask God for the gift of interpretation, so that the tongue can benefit others.

For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays but my mind is unfruitful. Key words. “My spirit”: the inner person moved by the Spirit. “Mind” (nous): understanding. “Unfruitful” (akarpos): produces no fruit, no understanding for himself or others.

What am I to do? Key words. Paul’s conclusion:

I will pray with my spirit, but I will pray with my mind also; I will sing praise with my spirit, but I will sing with my mind also. Key words. Both spirit and mind. Worship should engage the whole person, heart and understanding. Singing with the mind means singing words we understand and mean (Colossians 3:16; Ephesians 5:19).

What it does not mean. It does not mean emotion is bad in worship. It means emotion must be joined to understanding.

In a sentence. So someone who speaks in a tongue should pray for the ability to interpret it. If Paul prays in a tongue, his spirit prays but his understanding gets nothing from it. So what will he do? He will pray with his spirit and with his understanding; he will sing with his spirit and with his understanding too.

For worship. Next time you sing in church, think about the words. Sing with your mind as well as your heart.

verseByVerse.quote: Otherwise, if you give thanks with your spirit, how can anyone in the position of an outsider say “Amen” to your thanksgiving when he does not know what you are saying? For you may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not being built up.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Otherwise, if you give thanks with your spirit, how can anyone in the position of an outsider say “Amen” to your thanksgiving when he does not know what you are saying? For you may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not being built up.

Otherwise, if you give thanks with your spirit. Key words. Praising God in a tongue.

How can anyone in the position of an outsider say “Amen” to your thanksgiving. Key words. “Amen” (so be it) was the congregation’s response to prayers, as in the synagogue (Nehemiah 8:6; Psalm 106:48). The outsider (idiōtēs, an ordinary person, uninstructed) cannot join in.

When he does not know what you are saying? Key words. You cannot say Amen to what you do not understand.

For you may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not being built up. Key words. The prayer itself may be fine before God, but it fails in its public purpose.

What it does not mean. It does not mean saying Amen is a mere formality. It is the whole congregation’s agreement with the prayer.

In a sentence. Otherwise, when you praise God in the spirit, how can someone who does not understand say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying? Your thanks may be fine, but the other person gains nothing from it.

On a Tuesday. When someone leads prayer in church, listen and say Amen from the heart.
verseByVerse.note: “Amen” (“so be it”) was the congregation’s response to prayer and thanksgiving.

verseByVerse.quote: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you. Nevertheless, in church I would rather speak five words with my mind in order to instruct others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
verseByVerse.commentary:
I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you. Nevertheless, in church I would rather speak five words with my mind in order to instruct others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.

I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you. Key words. Paul is not criticising tongues out of jealousy or lack. He had the gift abundantly.

Nevertheless, in church I would rather speak five words with my mind in order to instruct others. Key words. In church: in the gathered congregation. “Instruct” (katēcheō, from which catechise): teach.

Than ten thousand words in a tongue. Key words. Ten thousand (myrioi, the largest Greek number word). Five understandable words are worth more than a flood of uninterpreted tongues.

What it does not mean. It does not mean Paul encouraged private tongues as a superior form of prayer. He simply says public worship is for understanding.

In a sentence. Paul thanks God that he speaks in tongues more than any of you. But in church he would rather speak five words that make sense and teach others than ten thousand words in a tongue.

For worship. Thank God for five clear words of truth that changed your life. Share some with someone today.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Paul urges them to stop thinking like children; they should be infants in evil but adults in their thinking. Scripture says that God would speak to his people through people of strange tongues and foreign lips, and even then they would not listen. So tongues are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers, while prophecy is for believers, not unbelievers. If the whole church meets and everyone speaks in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers come in, they will say the believers are out of their minds. But if everyone prophesies and an unbeliever or outsider comes in, he will be convicted and judged by all, the secrets of his heart will be laid bare, and he will fall down and worship God, declaring that God is really among them.
verseByVerse.theology:
Worship and Witness

Paul’s concern for the unbeliever who might walk in to the church meeting is a significant ecclesiological statement: corporate worship is not only for the already-converted. The community that worships in such a way that the outsider can be addressed, convicted, and drawn to worship is doing something the tongues-heavy meeting cannot do. This does not make evangelism the primary purpose of corporate worship — the primary purpose is the glorification of God — but it recognises that intelligible worship of the living God is inherently missionary in its effect.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: The Corinthian meetings were apparently chaotic — multiple tongues-speakers simultaneously, no interpretation, no order. Paul’s Isaiah citation turns their spiritual pride upside down: the tongues without interpretation is a sign associated with divine judgment, not divine favour. Now: The church that makes its corporate worship impenetrable to the outsider — whether through uninterpreted ecstatic experience, impenetrable theological jargon, or cultural inscrutability — is failing the unbeliever who walks through the door. The word of God should be the thing that disturbs, not the incomprehensibility of the proceedings.

verseByVerse.quote: Brothers, do not be children in your thinking. Be infants in evil, but in your thinking be mature. In the Law it is written, “By people of strange tongues and by the lips of foreigners will I speak to this people, and even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.” Thus tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers, while prophecy is a sign not for unbelievers but for believers.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Brothers, do not be children in your thinking. Be infants in evil, but in your thinking be mature. In the Law it is written, “By people of strange tongues and by the lips of foreigners will I speak to this people, and even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.” Thus tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers, while prophecy is a sign not for unbelievers but for believers.

Brothers, do not be children in your thinking. Key words. The Corinthians’ fascination with tongues was childish (13:11).

Be infants in evil, but in your thinking be mature. Key words. Be innocent like babies about evil, but grown up in understanding (Romans 16:19; Matthew 10:16).

In the Law it is written. Key words. “The Law” here means the Scriptures. In Isaiah, foreign speech was a sign of judgement: Israel refused to listen to God’s clear word through the prophets, so God would speak to them through the unintelligible language of Assyrian invaders (Isaiah 28:11–12; Deuteronomy 28:49).

“By people of strange tongues and by the lips of foreigners will I speak to this people, and even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.” Key words. Foreign tongues were God’s judgement on unbelief.

Thus tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers. Key words. A sign of judgement. When unbelievers hear tongues they cannot understand, it confirms them in their unbelief and alienation. At Pentecost, tongues also signalled that the gospel was going to the nations, and judgement was coming on unbelieving Israel.

While prophecy is a sign not for unbelievers but for believers. Key words. Prophecy shows God’s presence and favour among believers. And as verses 24–25 show, it also brings unbelievers to faith.

What it does not mean. It does not mean tongues were meant to convert unbelievers. Paul says uninterpreted tongues make outsiders think the church is mad (v. 23).

In a sentence. Brothers and sisters, stop thinking like children. Be babies when it comes to evil, but adults in your thinking. The law says, “Through people of foreign speech and through the lips of strangers I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.” So tongues are a sign, not for believers but for unbelievers; prophecy, however, is for believers, not unbelievers.

For worship. Thank God that he speaks to you clearly in his word. Do not harden your heart to it.
verseByVerse.note: “The Law” here means the Scriptures. In Isaiah, foreign speech — the Assyrian invaders — was a sign of judgment on those who refused to listen.

parallels.desc: by people of strange lips and with a foreign tongue the LORD will speak to this people

verseByVerse.quote: If, therefore, the whole church comes together and all speak in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds? But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or outsider enters, he is convicted by all, he is called to account by all,
verseByVerse.commentary:
If, therefore, the whole church comes together and all speak in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds? But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or outsider enters, he is convicted by all, he is called to account by all,

If, therefore, the whole church comes together and all speak in tongues. Key words. The whole church: the gathering of all the house churches. All speaking in tongues: the chaos Paul is correcting.

And outsiders or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds? Key words. “Out of your minds” (mainomai, mad, raving). Like the frenzy of pagan cults. Unbelievers often attended Christian gatherings; worship should be understandable to them.

But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or outsider enters. Key words. If all speak God’s word intelligibly, one by one (v. 31),

He is convicted by all. Key words. “Convicted” (elenchō, exposed, shown his sin, as the Spirit convicts, John 16:8).

He is called to account by all. Key words. “Called to account” (anakrinō, examined, searched). God’s word through his people searches him.

What it does not mean. It does not mean worship should be designed mainly for unbelievers. It should be clear, so that unbelievers present understand and are confronted.

In a sentence. So if the whole church meets and everyone speaks in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers come in, won’t they say you are mad? But if everyone is prophesying and an unbeliever or outsider comes in, he will be convicted of sin by all and brought under judgement by all,

On a Tuesday. Invite an unbelieving friend to church. Pray that God will speak to them through his word.

verseByVerse.quote: the secrets of his heart are disclosed, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God and declare that God is really among you.
verseByVerse.commentary:
the secrets of his heart are disclosed, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God and declare that God is really among you.

The secrets of his heart are disclosed. Key words. God’s word exposes hidden thoughts (Hebrews 4:12). The unbeliever feels: this is about me. God knows me.

And so, falling on his face, he will worship God. Key words. The posture of awe and surrender (Isaiah 45:14; Zechariah 8:23).

And declare that God is really among you. Key words. From Isaiah 45:14: surely God is in you. The goal of worship: outsiders recognise God’s presence. Not through chaos or showmanship, but through his word convicting hearts.

What it does not mean. It does not mean prophecy is the only way unbelievers are converted. Preaching the gospel does the same today.

In a sentence. and the secrets of his heart will be laid bare. Then he will fall down and worship God, exclaiming, “God is really here among you!”

For worship. Pray that your church’s worship would be so filled with God’s word that visitors say: God is really here.

parallels.desc: God is with you only
we have heard that God is with you

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 26–40 — Orderly Worship and Final Rules
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: When they meet, each person may bring a hymn, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue or an interpretation, but everything must be done to build up the church. If anyone speaks in a tongue, there should be two, or at most three, one at a time, and someone must interpret; without an interpreter the speaker should keep quiet in church and speak to himself and to God. Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh what is said. If a revelation comes to someone else who is sitting there, the first speaker should stop. They can all prophesy in turn, so that everyone learns and is encouraged. The spirits of prophets are under the prophets’ control, because God is not a God of disorder but of peace. As in all the churches of the saints, women are to keep silent in the assemblies; they are not allowed to speak but should be in submission, as the law also says. If they want to learn something, they should ask their husbands at home, for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church. Did the word of God begin with the Corinthians, or are they the only people it has reached? Anyone who thinks he is a prophet or spiritual should acknowledge that what Paul writes is the Lord’s command. Anyone who ignores this will himself be ignored. So they should eagerly desire to prophesy and not forbid speaking in tongues, but everything should be done in a fitting and orderly way.
verseByVerse.theology:
God as the Ground of Ordered Worship

The theological ground for orderly worship — “God is not a God of confusion but of peace” — is a direct application of the doctrine of God to liturgical practice. The triune God is the most perfectly ordered being there is: the three persons in eternal, loving, ordered communion. Worship that is chaotic and disorderly is, at a deep level, a misrepresentation of the God being worshipped. Conversely, worship that is ordered, intelligible, and participatory is an enacted icon of the divine order. The Reformers understood this: the liturgical reforms of Geneva and Zurich were not mere preference but a theological conviction that worship should reflect the character of the God it addresses.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: The Corinthian meeting was apparently chaotic: multiple simultaneous tongues, no weighing of prophecies, a general air of competitive spiritual display. Paul’s practical rules — two or three, in turn, with evaluation — are not bureaucratic restrictions but pastoral wisdom about how a community can actually benefit from the gifts God has given it. Now: “Decently and in order” is the guiding principle for every aspect of church life, from Sunday worship to congregational meetings to pastoral care. Order is not the suppression of the Spirit; it is the condition in which the Spirit’s gifts can be received and used by the whole community.

verseByVerse.quote: What then, brothers? When you come together, each one has a hymn, a lesson, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. Let all things be done for building up.
verseByVerse.commentary:
What then, brothers? When you come together, each one has a hymn, a lesson, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. Let all things be done for building up.

What then, brothers? Key words. Paul now gives practical instructions.

When you come together, each one has a hymn, a lesson, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. Key words. A picture of early Christian worship, with many participating. A hymn (psalmos, perhaps a psalm or new song). A lesson (didachē, teaching). A revelation: a prophecy. A tongue and interpretation.

Let all things be done for building up. Key words. The rule for everything (oikodomē).

Where Christians differ: how should worship be ordered? Some take this verse as the model for open, participatory worship, with anyone contributing. Others hold to the regulative principle: worship should include only what God commands, led by qualified men. Verdict: The apostolic church had more open participation, partly because of the revelatory gifts then active. With the canon closed and those gifts ceased, the core elements of worship are those God has appointed: reading and preaching the Scriptures, prayer, singing psalms, hymns and spiritual songs, the sacraments, and giving (Westminster 21.5). Worship should be ordered, led by those God has called, and above all edifying. Within that, the congregation participates fully in singing, prayer and Amen.

What it does not mean. It does not mean worship should be a free-for-all. Order is required (v. 40).

In a sentence. What then, brothers and sisters? When you gather, one has a song, another a teaching, another a revelation, a tongue or an interpretation. Everything must be done to build up the church.

For worship. Come to church ready to contribute: with a heart to sing, pray and listen, aiming to build others up.

verseByVerse.quote: If any speak in a tongue, let there be only two or at most three, and each in turn, and let someone interpret. But if there is no one to interpret, let each of them keep silent in church and speak to himself and to God.
verseByVerse.commentary:
If any speak in a tongue, let there be only two or at most three, and each in turn, and let someone interpret. But if there is no one to interpret, let each of them keep silent in church and speak to himself and to God.

If any speak in a tongue, let there be only two or at most three. Key words. Limits. Not a whole service of tongues.

And each in turn. Key words. One at a time, not all together.

And let someone interpret. Key words. Always with interpretation.

But if there is no one to interpret, let each of them keep silent in church. Key words. No interpreter, no tongue. Speakers must control themselves.

And speak to himself and to God. Key words. Quietly, privately, in his own heart.

What it does not mean. It does not mean speakers are overwhelmed and cannot help it. The gift was under the speaker’s control.

In a sentence. If anyone speaks in a tongue, two or at most three should speak, one after another, and someone must interpret. If there is no interpreter, the speaker should keep quiet in the church and speak only to himself and God.

On a Tuesday. Spiritual zeal never excuses disorder. Self-control is a fruit of the Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is said. If a revelation is made to another sitting there, let the first be silent. For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all be encouraged,
verseByVerse.commentary:
Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is said. If a revelation is made to another sitting there, let the first be silent. For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all be encouraged,

Let two or three prophets speak. Key words. Limits for prophecy too.

And let the others weigh what is said. Key words. “Weigh” (diakrinō, evaluate, discern). New Testament prophecy was not automatically accepted. It had to be tested against apostolic teaching (1 Thessalonians 5:20–21; 1 John 4:1). This shows that Corinthian congregational prophecy differed from the authority of Scripture, which is not weighed but obeyed.

If a revelation is made to another sitting there, let the first be silent. Key words. Courtesy and order: one speaker at a time.

For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all be encouraged. Key words. Taking turns allows everyone with a word to give it, and everyone to benefit.

What it does not mean. It does not mean everyone in the church was a prophet (12:29). All who had the gift could take their turn.

In a sentence. Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should carefully weigh what is said. If a revelation comes to someone else who is sitting there, the first speaker should stop. You can all prophesy in turn, so that everyone may learn and be encouraged,

For worship. Weigh everything you hear in church, and everywhere else, by Scripture.

parallels.desc: test everything

verseByVerse.quote: and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets. For God is not a God of confusion but of peace. As in all the churches of the saints,
verseByVerse.commentary:
and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets. For God is not a God of confusion but of peace. As in all the churches of the saints,

And the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets. Key words. Prophets are not overpowered by the Spirit. They can control when and whether they speak. Unlike pagan frenzy, the Holy Spirit does not override the person.

For God is not a God of confusion but of peace. Key words. “Confusion” (akatastasia, disorder, chaos). God’s character shapes worship. He is a God of order and peace; worship that is chaotic misrepresents him.

As in all the churches of the saints. Key words. This phrase may end the sentence about God’s peace, or begin the next about women (ESV). Either way: Corinth must conform to the practice of all the churches.

What it does not mean. It does not mean worship should be dull or rigid. Order serves peace and joy.

In a sentence. Prophets are in control of their own spirits, because God is not a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of God’s people.

On a Tuesday. Bring peace and order to your home and work, as reflections of the God of peace.

verseByVerse.quote: the women should keep silent in the churches. For they are not permitted to speak, but should be in submission, as the Law also says. If there is anything they desire to learn, let them ask their husbands at home. For it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.
verseByVerse.commentary:
the women should keep silent in the churches. For they are not permitted to speak, but should be in submission, as the Law also says. If there is anything they desire to learn, let them ask their husbands at home. For it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.

The women should keep silent in the churches. Key words. Paul has already assumed that women pray and prophesy in worship (11:5), so this cannot be total silence. The context is the weighing of prophecies (v. 29). Women should not take part in that public judging and questioning, which carried teaching authority over the congregation.

For they are not permitted to speak, but should be in submission, as the Law also says. Key words. Probably a reference to the creation order in Genesis 2, as in 1 Timothy 2:13 and 1 Corinthians 11:8–9. The principle is headship, not culture alone.

If there is anything they desire to learn, let them ask their husbands at home. Key words. Wives questioning or challenging prophets (perhaps their own husbands) in public would undermine order and headship. Paul directs their questions to the home, assuming women should learn.

For it is shameful for a woman to speak in church. Key words. Speak here in the sense of the public judging and questioning just described.

Where Christians differ: women’s silence. Some take this as an absolute ban on women speaking at all in church. Others say it was a cultural rule for disruptive Corinthian women and no longer applies, or even that it was not written by Paul. Verdict: The verses are in all the manuscripts, though a few move them after verse 40. Since Paul allows women to pray and prophesy (11:5), this is not a ban on all speech, but on women taking the role of authoritatively judging prophecy and teaching in the gathered church, which belongs to qualified men (1 Timothy 2:11–12). This is the complementarian position. Women may sing, pray, testify, and serve in countless ways. The principle is grounded in creation, not merely culture.

What it does not mean. It does not mean women are less intelligent or spiritual, or that their questions are unwelcome. Paul wants them to learn.

In a sentence. women should not speak in the churches when prophecies are being judged. They are not given that role, but should accept the order the law teaches. If they want to ask about something, they should ask their husbands at home, for it is not fitting for a woman to take that part in the church.

On a Tuesday. Husbands, be ready to discuss Scripture with your wives at home. Make your home a place of learning together.
verseByVerse.note: Paul has already assumed that women pray and prophesy in worship (11:5). Interpreters differ on what speaking is forbidden here; many take it as the public judging of prophecies just mentioned (v. 29).

verseByVerse.quote: Or was it from you that the word of God came? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
verseByVerse.commentary:
Or was it from you that the word of God came? Or are you the only ones it has reached?

Or was it from you that the word of God came? Key words. Sharp irony. The Corinthians acted as if they were the source of God’s word, free to make their own rules. They were not.

Or are you the only ones it has reached? Key words. They were one church among many, receiving the same word, and must follow the same practice (v. 33).

What it does not mean. It does not mean local churches have no freedom in practical matters. It means they cannot overrule apostolic teaching.

In a sentence. Did the word of God begin with you? Are you the only people it has reached?

For worship. Receive God’s word humbly. You did not invent it; you received it.

verseByVerse.quote: If anyone thinks that he is a prophet, or spiritual, he should acknowledge that the things I am writing to you are a command of the Lord. If anyone does not recognize this, he is not recognized.
verseByVerse.commentary:
If anyone thinks that he is a prophet, or spiritual, he should acknowledge that the things I am writing to you are a command of the Lord. If anyone does not recognize this, he is not recognized.

If anyone thinks that he is a prophet, or spiritual. Key words. Those who claim spiritual gifts.

He should acknowledge that the things I am writing to you are a command of the Lord. Key words. A strong claim to authority. Paul’s writing is the Lord’s command. A true prophet will recognise apostolic authority. Any prophecy that contradicts the apostle is false. This shows that the apostolic writings, now our New Testament, stand above all claimed revelation.

If anyone does not recognize this, he is not recognized. Key words. Not recognised by God, or by the church as a true prophet.

What it does not mean. It does not mean Paul was arrogant. He speaks as Christ’s appointed apostle.

In a sentence. Anyone who thinks he is a prophet or spiritually gifted should recognise that what Paul is writing is the Lord’s command. Anyone who ignores this will himself be ignored.

On a Tuesday. Test every claimed word from God, every feeling, every teaching, by Scripture. Scripture is the Lord’s command.

verseByVerse.quote: So, my brothers, earnestly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues. But all things should be done decently and in order.
verseByVerse.commentary:
So, my brothers, earnestly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues. But all things should be done decently and in order.

So, my brothers, earnestly desire to prophesy. Key words. The summary. Prophecy is to be desired.

And do not forbid speaking in tongues. Key words. Tongues, rightly used with interpretation, were a genuine gift then.

But all things should be done decently and in order. Key words. “Decently” (euschēmonōs, fittingly, beautifully). “In order” (kata taxin, in proper order, like soldiers in ranks). The final word on worship.

Where Christians differ: does “do not forbid tongues” apply today? Continuationists argue that churches today must not forbid tongues. Verdict: Paul’s command applied when the gift was active. If the revelatory and sign gifts have ceased with the apostolic age, as argued on 12:10, the question is whether present-day phenomena are the same gift. Cessationists believe they are not. Churches should neither mock nor exclude continuationist believers, and all should agree on the principles here: everything must be understood, edifying, tested by Scripture, orderly, and done in love.

What it does not mean. It does not mean order is opposed to the Spirit. The Spirit is the author of order.

In a sentence. So, brothers and sisters, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues. But everything should be done in a fitting and orderly way.

For worship. Thank God for orderly, edifying worship. Pray for your church’s gatherings to honour him.

14.text: <sup>1</sup>Pursue love, and earnestly desire the spiritual gifts, especially that you may prophesy.<sup>2</sup>For one who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men but to God; for no one understands him, but he utters mysteries in the Spirit.<sup>3</sup>On the other hand, the one who prophesies speaks to people for their upbuilding and encouragement and consolation.<sup>4</sup>The one who speaks in a tongue builds up himself, but the one who prophesies builds up the church.<sup>5</sup>Now I want you all to speak in tongues, but even more to prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless someone interprets, so that the church may be built up.<sup>6</sup>Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?<sup>7</sup>If even lifeless instruments, such as the flute or the harp, do not give distinct notes, how will anyone know what is played?<sup>8</sup>And if the bugle gives an indistinct sound, who will get ready for battle?<sup>9</sup>So with yourselves, if with your tongue you utter speech that is not intelligible, how will anyone know what is said? For you will be speaking into the air.<sup>10</sup>There are doubtless many different languages in the world, and none is without meaning,<sup>11</sup>but if I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be a foreigner to the speaker and the speaker a foreigner to me.<sup>12</sup>So with yourselves, since you are eager for manifestations of the Spirit, strive to excel in building up the church.<sup>13</sup>Therefore, one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.<sup>14</sup>For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays but my mind is unfruitful.<sup>15</sup>What am I to do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will pray with my mind also; I will sing praise with my spirit, but I will sing with my mind also.<sup>16</sup>Otherwise, if you give thanks with your spirit, how can anyone in the position of an outsider say “Amen” to your thanksgiving when he does not know what you are saying?<sup>17</sup>For you may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not being built up.<sup>18</sup>I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.<sup>19</sup>Nevertheless, in church I would rather speak five words with my mind in order to instruct others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.<sup>20</sup>Brothers, do not be children in your thinking. Be infants in evil, but in your thinking be mature.<sup>21</sup>In the Law it is written, “By people of strange tongues and by the lips of foreigners will I speak to this people, and even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.”<sup>22</sup>Thus tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers, while prophecy is a sign not for unbelievers but for believers.<sup>23</sup>If, therefore, the whole church comes together and all speak in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds?<sup>24</sup>But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or outsider enters, he is convicted by all, he is called to account by all,<sup>25</sup>the secrets of his heart are disclosed, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God and declare that God is really among you.<sup>26</sup>What then, brothers? When you come together, each one has a hymn, a lesson, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. Let all things be done for building up.<sup>27</sup>If any speak in a tongue, let there be only two or at most three, and each in turn, and let someone interpret.<sup>28</sup>But if there is no one to interpret, let each of them keep silent in church and speak to himself and to God.<sup>29</sup>Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is said.<sup>30</sup>If a revelation is made to another sitting there, let the first be silent.<sup>31</sup>For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all be encouraged,<sup>32</sup>and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.<sup>33</sup>For God is not a God of confusion but of peace. As in all the churches of the saints,<sup>34</sup>the women should keep silent in the churches. For they are not permitted to speak, but should be in submission, as the Law also says.<sup>35</sup>If there is anything they desire to learn, let them ask their husbands at home. For it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.<sup>36</sup>Or was it from you that the word of God came? Or are you the only ones it has reached?<sup>37</sup>If anyone thinks that he is a prophet, or spiritual, he should acknowledge that the things I am writing to you are a command of the Lord.<sup>38</sup>If anyone does not recognize this, he is not recognized.<sup>39</sup>So, my brothers, earnestly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.<sup>40</sup>But all things should be done decently and in order.

15.title: The Resurrection of the Dead
15.overview:
Some in Corinth were saying there is no resurrection of the dead. That fitted Greek thinking well. Many Greeks regarded the body as a prison for the soul; a philosophical pun called the body (sōma) a tomb (sēma). Salvation meant the soul escaping, not the corpse rising, and the Athenians laughed when Paul spoke of resurrection (Acts 17:32). In one of Aeschylus’ tragedies the god Apollo says that once a man has died and the dust has soaked up his blood, there is no rising again. The Corinthians probably still believed in Christ’s resurrection and in some spiritual life after death, but not in the raising of their own bodies.

Paul answers in four stages. First, the facts: Christ died for our sins, was buried, was raised on the third day and appeared to Peter, the Twelve, more than five hundred at once, James, all the apostles and finally Paul. Second, the consequences: if there is no resurrection, Christ was not raised, preaching and faith are empty, sins unforgiven, the dead lost, and Christians the most pitiable of people. Third, the plan: Christ has been raised as the firstfruits of the harvest; as all die in Adam, all in Christ will be made alive; he reigns until every enemy, death last of all, is defeated. Fourth, the body: like a seed and the plant that grows from it, the body sown in weakness will be raised in power, a body fitted for the Spirit, bearing the image of the last Adam. At the last trumpet the dead will rise and the living be changed, death will be swallowed up in victory, and so believers’ labour in the Lord is never in vain.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–11 — The Resurrection of Christ: The Apostolic Testimony
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Paul reminds them of the gospel he preached, which they received and on which they stand, and by which they are saved if they hold firmly to it, unless they believed in vain. He handed on to them, as of first importance, what he himself had received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures, and that he appeared to Peter and then to the Twelve. After that he appeared to more than five hundred believers at once, most of whom are still living, though some have died. Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles, and last of all to Paul, as to one abnormally born. Paul is the least of the apostles and does not deserve the name, because he persecuted God’s church. But by God’s grace he is what he is, and that grace was not wasted; he worked harder than all of them, though it was God’s grace with him. Whether it was Paul or they, this is what they preached and what the Corinthians believed.
verseByVerse.theology:
The Resurrection as the Foundation of Salvation

Paul’s phrase “Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures” is among the earliest creedal formulations we possess, pre-dating the letter (Paul received it). The resurrection “in accordance with the Scriptures” grounds both events in OT prophecy — Psalm 16:10, Isaiah 53, Hosea 6:2 being the primary candidates. The conjunction of death and resurrection is crucial: the resurrection is not an isolated miracle but the divine vindication of the atoning death. Without the resurrection, the death has no declared meaning; without the death, the resurrection has no redemptive content. Together they constitute the gospel.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: The Greek philosophical tradition was deeply ambivalent about bodily resurrection. The famous scene in Acts 17:32 — when Paul mentions the resurrection, some mock and some are interested — captures the standard Hellenistic reaction. The Platonic tradition prized the release of the soul from the body; the idea of the body being raised was not an upgrade but a retrogression to the bodily existence the soul was trying to escape. Paul’s case for the resurrection runs directly against this deeply embedded cultural instinct. Now: The modern version of the Greek objection is not philosophical but scientific: dead bodies do not rise. Paul’s answer is the same: the evidence of the witnesses. The question is not whether bodies normally rise but whether this specific body, on this specific morning, was raised by the God who created bodies in the first place.

verseByVerse.quote: Now I would remind you, brothers, of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, in which you stand, and by which you are being saved, if you hold fast to the word I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Now I would remind you, brothers, of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, in which you stand, and by which you are being saved, if you hold fast to the word I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.

Meaning first. 1 Corinthians 15 is the Bible’s fullest teaching on the resurrection. Some in Corinth, shaped by Greek thought that saw the body as worthless or a prison, were denying that believers will be raised bodily. Paul answers in five movements. First, the gospel itself rests on the bodily resurrection of Christ, attested by Scripture and by hundreds of eyewitnesses, including Paul (vv. 1–11). Second, if the dead are not raised, then Christ was not raised, faith is useless, sins are unforgiven, the dead are lost, and Christians are the most pitiable people alive (vv. 12–19). Third, Christ has in fact been raised as the firstfruits of the harvest; as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive. He reigns now until every enemy, death last of all, is destroyed, and then he hands the kingdom to the Father (vv. 20–28). Fourth, the practical consequences: why else would believers risk their lives, or live holy lives (vv. 29–34)? Fifth, what will the resurrection body be like? Like a seed and the plant, it will be the same person, transformed: imperishable, glorious, powerful, spiritual, bearing the image of Christ, the last Adam (vv. 35–49). At the last trumpet, the dead will be raised and the living changed in an instant, and death will be swallowed up in victory. So be steadfast, for your labour in the Lord is not in vain (vv. 50–58).

Setting and background. Some at Corinth were denying the future resurrection of the dead (v. 12). Greeks generally believed the soul might survive, but bodily resurrection seemed absurd (Acts 17:32). Some Corinthians may also have thought that they had already been raised spiritually and needed nothing more (4:8; 2 Timothy 2:18).

Now I would remind you, brothers, of the gospel I preached to you. Key words. “Remind” (gnōrizō, make known again). Not a new teaching, but the gospel they already knew.

Which you received, in which you stand. Key words. They received it by faith, and it is the ground they stand on.

And by which you are being saved. Key words. Present tense: salvation is ongoing, to be completed in the resurrection.

If you hold fast to the word I preached to you—unless you believed in vain. Key words. “Hold fast” (katechō): keep a firm grip. “In vain” (eikē, without cause, without result). If the resurrection is false, their believing was pointless. Or: if they let go of this gospel, they show their faith was empty.

What it does not mean. It does not mean salvation depends on our grip rather than God’s. True faith perseveres because God keeps it (1:8–9). But those who abandon the gospel show their faith was never real.

In a sentence. Brothers and sisters, Paul wants to remind you of the gospel he preached to you: you received it, you are standing on it, and through it you are being saved, as long as you keep holding firmly to the message he preached; otherwise your believing was for nothing.

On a Tuesday. Hold fast to the gospel today. Remind yourself of it: Christ died for your sins and was raised.
verseByVerse.note: Some at Corinth were denying the future resurrection of the body; most Greeks thought the body was left behind at death.

verseByVerse.quote: For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures,
verseByVerse.commentary:
For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures,

For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received. Key words. Verses 3–5 are an early summary of the faith that Paul had received, probably soon after his conversion, around AD 35, within a few years of the crucifixion. “Delivered” and “received” are terms for passing on tradition (11:23). “Of first importance”: at the very heart of the gospel.

That Christ died for our sins. Key words. “For” (hyper, on behalf of, in place of). His death dealt with our sins: he bore the penalty we deserved.

In accordance with the Scriptures. Key words. As the Old Testament foretold: especially Isaiah 53:5–12, the servant wounded for our transgressions. The cross was God’s plan, not an accident.

That he was buried. Key words. Burial proves he really died. And it means the resurrection was bodily: the body placed in the tomb was the body raised, leaving the tomb empty.

That he was raised on the third day. Key words. “Was raised” (egēgertai, perfect tense passive): God raised him, and he remains raised. On the third day: a specific, historical date.

In accordance with the Scriptures. Key words. Psalm 16:10, Isaiah 53:10–12, Hosea 6:2, and the sign of Jonah (Matthew 12:40).

Where Christians differ: the meaning of Christ’s death. Some see Christ’s death mainly as an example of love, or as a victory over evil powers, and reject the idea that he bore the punishment for sins. Verdict: Christ died for our sins. Scripture presents his death as many things, including example and victory, but at its heart it is penal substitution: he stood in our place, bearing the penalty of God’s just wrath against our sins, so that we might be forgiven and declared righteous (Isaiah 53:5–6; Romans 3:25–26; 2 Corinthians 5:21; Galatians 3:13). This is of first importance.

What it does not mean. It does not mean the resurrection was a spiritual idea or vision. The burial and empty tomb rule that out.

In a sentence. For what Paul received he passed on to you as most important: Christ died for our sins as the Scriptures foretold; he was buried; and he was raised on the third day, as the Scriptures foretold;

For worship. Recite this gospel slowly as a prayer of thanks: Christ died for my sins, was buried, and was raised.
verseByVerse.note: Verses 3–5 are an early summary of the faith that Paul had received — within a few years of the resurrection.

verseByVerse.quote: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
verseByVerse.commentary:
and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.

And that he appeared to Cephas. Key words. Cephas is Peter. Jesus appeared to Peter individually on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:34). The man who had denied him was the first apostle to see him risen: an act of grace and restoration.

Then to the twelve. Key words. “The twelve” was the title of the group even when Judas was gone and Thomas was absent at the first appearance (John 20:19–29). The apostolic group as a whole saw him.

What it does not mean. It does not mean these were inner visions or hallucinations. “Appeared” (ōphthē, was seen) describes real sightings. Jesus ate with them and they touched him (Luke 24:39–43; John 20:27).

In a sentence. and that he was seen by Peter, and then by the Twelve.

On a Tuesday. Jesus appeared first to the apostle who had failed him most. If you have failed him, he still comes to you.
verseByVerse.note: Cephas is Peter. “The twelve” was the title of the group even when only eleven were present.

verseByVerse.quote: Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time, most of whom are still alive, though some have fallen asleep. Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time, most of whom are still alive, though some have fallen asleep. Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.

Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time. Key words. A mass appearance, probably in Galilee (Matthew 28:16–17). Hallucinations are private; five hundred people do not share the same hallucination.

Most of whom are still alive. Key words. Many of the five hundred could still be questioned when Paul wrote, about twenty years later. Paul is in effect saying: go and ask them. He is inviting investigation.

Though some have fallen asleep. Key words. Some had died. “Fallen asleep” is the Christian word for believers’ death: temporary, to be followed by waking at the resurrection.

Then he appeared to James. Key words. James, the brother of Jesus, who had not believed during Jesus’ ministry (John 7:5). The appearance converted him, and he became leader of the Jerusalem church (Acts 15:13; Galatians 1:19).

Then to all the apostles. Key words. Perhaps at the ascension (Acts 1:3–9), including a wider group beyond the Twelve.

Where Christians differ: soul sleep. Some take fallen asleep to mean that the dead are unconscious until the resurrection. Verdict: Sleep describes the appearance of the body in death and the certainty of waking. But Scripture teaches that the souls of believers go immediately into the presence of Christ, conscious and at rest, awaiting the resurrection of the body (Luke 23:43; 2 Corinthians 5:8; Philippians 1:23; Revelation 6:9–11; Westminster 32.1).

What it does not mean. It does not mean these were the only appearances. Paul gives an official list of witnesses.

In a sentence. After that he was seen by over five hundred brothers and sisters at once, most of whom are still living, though some have died. Then he was seen by James, then by all the apostles,

For worship. Your faith rests on public, testable history. Thank God for the eyewitnesses who saw the risen Lord.
verseByVerse.note: Many of the five hundred could still be questioned when Paul wrote. James is the Lord’s brother, who had not believed during Jesus’ ministry.

verseByVerse.quote: Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me. For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me. For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

Last of all. Key words. Paul was the last person to whom the risen Christ appeared in this way. The resurrection appearances ended with him.

As to one untimely born, he appeared also to me. Key words. “Untimely born” (ektrōma) describes an abnormal birth: a miscarriage or stillbirth, or a premature birth. Paul’s sudden, violent conversion on the Damascus road (Acts 9:3–6) came outside the normal time of the appearances. Perhaps his opponents called him a freak; he takes the insult on himself.

For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle. Key words. True humility. Paul never forgot what he had been.

Because I persecuted the church of God. Key words. He had hunted, imprisoned and helped kill believers (Acts 8:3; 22:4; 26:10–11; Galatians 1:13).

What it does not mean. It does not mean Paul’s apostleship was inferior or doubtful. He saw the risen Christ and was commissioned by him. It means he knew he did not deserve it.

In a sentence. and last of all he was seen by Paul too, as by someone born at the wrong time. For Paul is the least of the apostles and does not even deserve to be called an apostle, because he persecuted the church of God.

On a Tuesday. Remember what you were before Christ found you. It will keep you humble and grateful.
verseByVerse.note: “Untimely born” describes an abnormal birth — Paul’s sudden, late calling.

verseByVerse.quote: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not in vain. On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me. Whether then it was I or they, so we preach and so you believed.
verseByVerse.commentary:
But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not in vain. On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me. Whether then it was I or they, so we preach and so you believed.

But by the grace of God I am what I am. Key words. One of the great sentences of the Bible. Everything Paul is, apostle, Christian, forgiven sinner, is God’s free gift.

And his grace toward me was not in vain. Key words. “In vain” (kenē, empty). Grace produced results in Paul.

On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them. Key words. Paul laboured more than the other apostles. Grace does not make people lazy; it makes them work (Philippians 2:12–13).

Though it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me. Key words. Even his hard work was grace at work in him. The balance of effort and grace: we work hard, and every bit of it is God’s grace.

Whether then it was I or they, so we preach and so you believed. Key words. All the apostles preach the same gospel of the resurrection. The Corinthians believed it.

What it does not mean. It does not mean grace makes human effort unnecessary. It means our effort is the fruit of grace, not the cause of it.

In a sentence. But by God’s grace Paul is what he is, and that grace was not wasted on him. He worked harder than all the others, yet not he, but the grace of God with him. So whether it was he or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.

For worship. Say it today: by the grace of God I am what I am. Then work hard, by his grace.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 12–19 — If Christ Has Not Been Raised
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: If the message is that Christ has been raised, how can some of them say there is no resurrection of the dead? If there is none, Christ has not been raised either; and if Christ has not been raised, the apostles’ preaching is useless and so is their faith. The apostles would be found to be false witnesses about God, since they testified that he raised Christ, which he did not do if the dead are not raised. If Christ has not been raised, their faith is futile and they are still in their sins, and those who have died believing in Christ are lost. If their hope in Christ is only for this life, they are more to be pitied than anyone.
verseByVerse.theology:
The Resurrection as the Confirmation of the Atonement

Paul’s logic in v. 17 — “if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile and you are still in your sins” — grounds the significance of the resurrection in its relationship to the atonement. The death of Christ atones; the resurrection of Christ confirms and declares the atonement accepted. This is why Romans 4:25 says Christ “was raised for our justification”: the resurrection is the Father’s “yes” to the Son’s atoning sacrifice. Without the resurrection, Good Friday is a tragedy; with the resurrection, Good Friday is the pivot of history.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: The Corinthian denial of bodily resurrection was probably influenced by Platonic body-soul dualism: if the soul is what matters, and it survives death, why would God re-attach it to a body? Paul’s argument is that this misunderstands both what salvation means (the redemption of the whole person, body and soul) and what happened to Christ (his body was raised, not merely his spirit). Now: The contemporary version of the Corinthian position often appears in Christian thinking that treats the soul’s going to heaven as the whole story and the resurrection as an afterthought. Paul’s insistence is that the resurrection body is the destination, and the intermediate state (soul in God’s presence before the resurrection) is the waiting room.

verseByVerse.quote: Now if Christ is proclaimed as raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead? But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised. And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith is in vain.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Now if Christ is proclaimed as raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead? But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised. And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith is in vain.

Now if Christ is proclaimed as raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead? Key words. The inconsistency. They accepted Christ’s resurrection but denied the resurrection of believers.

But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised. Key words. If resurrection is impossible in principle, it did not happen to Christ either. Christ’s resurrection and ours stand or fall together.

And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith is in vain. Key words. “In vain” (kenos, empty). The whole message would be hollow. Christianity is not a set of moral teachings that work whether or not they are true. It rests on a historical event. If Christ is not raised, there is nothing left.

What it does not mean. It does not mean the resurrection is a matter of opinion. Paul treats it as fact, testable by witnesses.

In a sentence. If we preach that Christ was raised from the dead, how can some of you say that the dead are not raised? If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised either. And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is empty and so is your faith.

On a Tuesday. Your faith is not a feeling or a philosophy. It rests on a fact: Christ is risen. Stand on that today.

verseByVerse.quote: We are even found to be misrepresenting God, because we testified about God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise if it is true that the dead are not raised. For if the dead are not raised, not even Christ has been raised. And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile and you are still in your sins.
verseByVerse.commentary:
We are even found to be misrepresenting God, because we testified about God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise if it is true that the dead are not raised. For if the dead are not raised, not even Christ has been raised. And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile and you are still in your sins.

We are even found to be misrepresenting God. Key words. Literally, false witnesses of God. If Christ was not raised, the apostles are liars, and liars about God.

Because we testified about God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise if it is true that the dead are not raised. Key words. The apostles’ testimony is either true or a lie. No middle ground. People do not usually die for what they know to be a lie, and the apostles suffered and died for this testimony.

For if the dead are not raised, not even Christ has been raised. Key words. Repeated for emphasis.

And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile. Key words. “Futile” (mataia, useless, without result).

And you are still in your sins. Key words. The resurrection is God’s declaration that Christ’s sacrifice was accepted (Romans 4:25). Without it, there is no proof that sin has been dealt with. You would still be guilty.
